title: Personal data minimization and privacy by design
when: An app or form collects names, emails, phones, locations, health or payment details, or a review asks whether personal data is handled well.
prompt:
Goal: Collect only what a feature needs, keep it only as long as needed, protect it, and let people export and delete it.
Steps:
1. Inventory every personal field: purpose, storage place, who sees it, retention; remove fields without a purpose.
2. Prefer weaker forms: birth year over birth date, city over address, an age checkbox over a document number.
3. Mark optional fields and explain next to each required personal field why it is needed.
4. Keep personal data out of URLs, logs, analytics events and error reports; log ids instead.
5. Separate personal fields from content in storage and restrict access.
6. Offer export (JSON) and delete, purge inactive records after a stated period, and write a plain language privacy note.
Quality bar:
- Each personal field maps to a feature.
- Nothing sensitive in query strings or console output.
- Deletion also covers backups, or says when they expire.
Pitfalls:
- Collecting everything "for later".
- Pre checked consent boxes.
- Forgotten copies in browser storage.
Verify:
- [ ] A data inventory table exists.
- [ ] Optional fields marked.
- [ ] Export and delete paths exist.
- [ ] No personal data in logs or URLs.
Output: docs/privacy-data.md with the inventory and retention rules, plus the matching form and storage changes.

examples.input: revisa se meu formulário de inscrição pede dados demais
examples.output: inventory table, drop CPF and full birth date, retention 12 months, export and delete buttons
